Son dönemde aralarında Çin adına casusluk yaptığı öne sürülen bir kadınla yaşadığı ilişki dahil evlilik dışı ilişkileriyle ilgili haberlerle gündeme gelen Huang, Nvidia 'dan ayrılmasının ardından ilk kez açıklama yaptı.
Geçen hafta boyunca arkadaşlarından, sektördeki meslektaşlarından ve daha önce hiç tanışmadığı insanlardan gördüğü sevgi ve destek karşısında derinden etkilendiğini belirten Huang, ailesine ve kendisine nezaket gösteren herkese teşekkür etti.
Huang, 53 yıl önce ABD 'ye geldiğini ve Amerikan vatandaşı olmanın hayatının en büyük armağanlarından ve en gurur duyduğu anlarından biri olduğunu belirterek, Nvidia'nın ise hayatını adadığı bir çalışma olduğunu ifade etti.
Jensen Huang, "Şirketi bugünkü konumuna meslektaşlarımla birlikte taşımak benim için bir ayrıcalık ve onurdu. Nvidia gibi bir şirketin kurulması ancak Amerika'da mümkün olabilirdi. Ülkemizi de Nvidia'yı da seviyorum." ifadelerini kullandı.
Nvidia'daki herkesten beklenen standartları karşılayamadığını ve özel hayatında ciddi hatalar yaptığını belirten Huang, Yönetim Kurulu için yarattığı sorunlardan dolayı derin pişmanlık duyduğunu aktardı.
Huang, hatalarının tüm sorumluluğunu üstlendiğini ve Yönetim Kurulunun yürüttüğü bağımsız soruşturmayla tam işbirliği yapmaya kararlı olduğunu vurguladı.
Görevinden ayrılmasının ardından Nvidia çalışanlarından, yatırımcılardan, iş ortaklarından ve müşterilerden CEO olarak geri dönmesi yönünde yoğun çağrılar geldiğini belirten Huang, şunları kaydetti:
"Şirket karmaşık teknoloji, piyasa, rekabet ve jeopolitik dinamiklerle mücadele ederken birçok kişi doğrudan benimle iletişime geçmeye devam ediyor. Nvidia, her nesilde bir kez ortaya çıkabilecek türden bir şirket. Yönetim Kurulu, geri dönmemin hissedarlarımızın, çalışanlarımızın, şirketin ve Amerika'nın çıkarları için en iyisi olacağına karar verirse bu çağrılara yanıt vermekten ve CEO olarak görevime dönmekten onur duyarım. İyi dileklerini paylaşan herkese bir kez daha teşekkür ederim. Desteğiniz karşısında derin bir minnettarlık duyuyorum."

Huang said he is ready to return as Nvidia CEO if the company’s board would like him back at the helm.
Jensen Huang, the former CEO of chipmaker Nvidia, has agreed to appear in transcribed interviews with several United States House committees on December 1, even as he has said he would be “honored” to resume his job if the company’s board would like him to.
On Tuesday, the House Foreign Affairs Committee announced the upcoming interviews, which will also include the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and the House Intelligence Committee.
The US tech giant’s General Counsel Tim Teter will appear before the same committees on December 2 . It was not immediately clear whether the men would attend in person or speak remotely.
“We look forward to hearing from Jensen Huang and Tim Teter on their roles in a potential breach of our national security,” Republican chairmen of the committees, Brian Mast, John Moolenaar and Rick Crawford, said in a statement.
“The American people need answers on Mr Huang and Nvidia’s role in allowing dangerous PRC [People’s Republic of China] actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal.”
Huang stepped down as Nvidia’s CEO on Thursday after reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy, raised questions over exports of the company’s advanced AI chips to China.
The lawmakers first called on Huang on November 5 to appear before the committees. That came amid initial reports from The New York Times that US authorities had started investigating Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, which buys artificial intelligence (AI) chips from Nvidia, and with whom Huang has admitted to having an affair.
US authorities have scrutinised Megaspeed over suspicions that it helped Beijing gain access to advanced AI chips that are barred from shipment to China.
The announcement comes as Huang has expressed a willingness to return to the company since resigning last Thursday.
“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said in a post on the social media platform X.
“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”
Huang’s comments come amid reports that tech industry insiders were pushing for his return to the company, alongside a petition with more than 177,000 people calling for his return.
“The board’s decision now sits between a founder who has publicly asked for his job back, a shareholder base with the means to force the question, and an administration split between a president open to his return and a Treasury secretary demanding an outsider,” Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives, said in a note provided to Al Jazeera.
At the same time, Nvidia has announced a board-level committee to oversee national security and export controls, marking the first major governance move since Huang resigned.
The National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, a former Goldman Sachs vice chair, Nvidia said. Directors Stephen Neal, former CEO of law firm Cooley, and John Dabiri, a Caltech professor, will also serve on the committee.
US President Donald Trump welcomed the move, calling the launch of a national security initiative a good idea.
Nvidia stock tumbled in midday trading on Tuesday. It was down more than 1.6 percent for the day, 11 percent over the previous five days and 29.2 percent over the previous month.

Jensen Huang said that he is open to returning as chief executive of Nvidia , five days after he resigned from the company .
In a statement published Tuesday morning on X, Huang said that since stepping down he has received an “ outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO.”
“If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” Huang wrote.
Huang also thanked people who showed “kindness” to him and his family and acknowledged “the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met.” He reiterated his love for America and Nvidia and his remorse for his unfaithfulness to his wife, which he also expressed in a company-wide email sent last week.
Huang resigned four days after Nvidia launched an internal investigation into an affair he had admitted to having with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who has no known relation to Jensen. Huang reportedly misled the company’s general counsel and chief marketing officer about the affair with Alice.
The day before Huang stepped down, The New York Times reported that he'd had a second affair with one of his direct reports at Nvidia. After his resignation, Reuters reported on an alleged third affair with another Nvidia employee. The company’s code of conduct discourages "personal relationships" that "may create a conflict of interest."
Colette Kress, Nvidia’s longtime chief financial officer, was installed as interim CEO upon Huang’s resignation.
The New York Times first reported Jensen’s association with Alice, also known as Huang Le, in October 2025. On November 6 of this year, citing an intelligence memo that reportedly circulated among Trump administration officials last spring, The New York Times and the Financial Times reported that intelligence officials believed Alice may be an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Trump administration officials, including tech executive and White House Science and Technology advisory council cochair David Sacks, have questioned whether Alice was associated with the MSS. The Chinese government has rejected claims that Alice spied for the nation.
WIRED reported last week that on the same day Huang resigned, Nvidia employees began using an existing petition to the board to call for his reinstatement . It gained more than 1,600 comments in just a few hours.
A separate, public petition titled “ Stand With Jensen ” similarly calls for the executive’s return. At the time of writing, it has more than 193,000 online signatures, including more than 11,000 self-identified current and former Nvidia employees and more than 100,000 self-identified shareholders. On Friday, Elon Musk said that he was going to sign the petition, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan claimed that he had signed.
President Donald Trump told reporters on Monday that he “would not mind” if Huang returned as CEO, adding that he believed Huang had “learned a big lesson.”
Nvidia’s board of directors, however, reportedly said on Monday that it was not considering reinstating Huang as CEO. On Tuesday, the board announced that it had established a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee “for board-level oversight of the company’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management.”

The highly classified network that the National Security Agency uses for its internal communications is down, according to six people familiar with the matter.
The network, called NSANet, allows employees to communicate classified information internally. At this point there is no evidence of a cyberattack, sources said.
As the agency works to understand the scope of the problem, it has enacted staggered arrivals for personnel, the sources said.
“The National Security Agency experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance,” the agency said in a statement on Tuesday afternoon. “While some internal systems were affected, mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational and our ability to defend national security continues. NSA’s infrastructure is designed with multiple layers of redundancy to maintain operations during planned maintenance or unexpected events.”
A source familiar with the matter told CNN that restoration of the network was ongoing but not yet complete.
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said later Tuesday afternoon that the NSA outage was the result of the agency applying a software patch to address major software vulnerabilities that were discovered last month.
“The patching that has gone on following that has caused some of these systems to not come back up when you patch them as expected,” Clayton said on Fox Business. “That is that is what has happened at the NSA today.”
The vulnerabilities Clayton were referring to are in PHP, a programming language that powers about 70% of the world’s websites. AI tools helped researchers exploit them, setting off a scramble by government agencies and corporations around the world to address the issue in recent weeks. The NSA itself urged organizations to apply software patches.
The flaws in PHP could allow hackers to break into websites and read memory that could contain sensitive information, like passwords.
Clayton said there is no sign that any of the recent tech outages, including that affecting the NSA, were the result of a cyberattack.
A current and a former US official said an outage at NSANet would not impact the agency’s ability to communicate urgent intelligence to President Donald Trump while he is traveling in Asia on Air Force One.
Both sources described multiple redundancies and backup networks that the government could use to communicate securely with the president who is currently in the Philippines before heading to China tomorrow for talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
NSANet is “more of a network of networks, and it’s unlikely that a full outage exists given the many redundancies in place,” a former senior NSA official told CNN. “It could impact analysis and reporting, but for highest priority requirements they would find a way to work those. So it is alarming, but likely not crippling.”
A voicemail inbox recording for NSA employees on Tuesday described the situation as a “code yellow,” the second-highest in a three-level system that governs whether NSA employees report for work at the agency’s Fort Meade, Maryland, headquarters or not. The recording told non-emergency personnel to arrive for work in a staggered manner and for emergency personnel to arrive as usual. The New York Times first reported that detail.
The outage at America’s most powerful intelligence agency comes on the heels of multiple major tech glitches affecting airlines and other corporations around the country.
All flights nationwide were grounded for hours on Friday after a massive systems failure, leading to thousands of flights being delayed or canceled. The Federal Aviation Administration traced the problem to a single router in Arkansas.
Meanwhile, a massive outage last week affecting Microsoft products left people around the world unable to access Outlook email and Team meetings.
And in recent weeks banks and other services have experienced outages, on Monday thousands of Chase Bank customers reported they had trouble using their online accounts.
There is no indication that the NSA, FAA or Microsoft outages were caused by a cyberattack. But they are stark examples of how tech failures can roil markets and potentially threaten national security.
The US shares intelligence with a group of countries in what is known as the Five Eyes intelligence-sharing alliance, which includes the US, UK, New Zealand, Australia and Canada. That intelligence sharing system has not been impacted as a result of the NSANet outage, according to a source from one of the countries and a former US intelligence official.
Tuesday’s outage was not the first time the NSA’s internal computer networks have suffered significant disruption. In 2000, a tech failure at the agency downed computers for nearly three days and interrupted the processing of intelligence at Fort Meade, an agency spokesperson said at the time.

Instagram is introducing a new tool to help creators protect their original videos, the Meta-owned company announced Tuesday. The feature, called “content protection,” is already available on Facebook and is designed to detect when creators’ original videos are being used without their permission. The company is also expanding the tool to address AI content, not just conventional reposting.
The announcement comes in response to creators’ concerns over how easily original content can be copied and redistributed across social media platforms, especially considering how generative AI has made it easier to manipulate existing videos.
Instagram says the content protection tool continuously scans Instagram for unauthorized uses of creators’ protected videos. When Instagram detects a match for one of a creator’s Reels uploaded by another user, it sends the creator an alert. Creators can then choose to block the video from being viewed on both Instagram and Facebook to hide the matched content. They can also choose to add an “original by” label on the content that links viewers of the matching video back to their original video.
Additionally, creators can choose to keep the match visible while monitoring its performance or release their claim on the reel, allowing it to remain visible on Meta’s platforms.
The tool will also begin detecting AI-generated videos that reuse audio from creators’ original content, even when the visuals have been altered. This update will initially be tested with a small group of creators in the coming weeks. The company plans to expand access to this feature to creators who enroll in content protection on both Instagram and Facebook.
Instagram says it’s exploring ways to limit the reach of accounts and content that repeatedly use AI tools to repost others’ work.
Creators who are eligible for content protection will see a notification in their activity feed. Once they enroll, every original video they post to Instagram going forward is automatically protected. They can also choose to retroactively protect eligible videos they’ve already posted by manually selecting them.
If creators have permitted certain profiles to use their work, such as their second profile or a brand, they can add them to their allow list so their videos won’t be flagged as matches.
Tuesday’s announcement marks another step in Instagram’s ongoing efforts to give creators greater control over their content and protect the originality of their work.

Waymo robotaxis are no longer allowed to operate on California freeways after the state’s Department of Motor Vehicles restricted the Alphabet-owned company’s operations following several incidents that raised safety concerns.
California’s DMV, which regulates the testing and deployment of autonomous vehicles in the state, issued the operational restrictions on Waymo on November 11. However, the restrictions weren’t made public until Tuesday. San Francisco Business Times was the first to report the order.
The DMV confirmed the new restrictions to TechCrunch, stating that the department took action after three Waymo autonomous vehicles entered an active construction closure on U.S. Route 101 near Burlingame, and another separate incident involving California Highway Patrol vehicles on Highway 280 in San Francisco.
Waymo has complied and is preventing its robotaxis from accessing freeways in any of the markets it operates in, including those outside of California. Waymo currently has commercial operations in 15 U.S. cities.
The DMV said Waymo’s freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety.
“The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present, despite a prior restriction and corrective actions implemented following similar incidents that occurred on May 18, 2026,” according to an emailed statement sent to TechCrunch.
The DMV said the restrictions will remain in place until Waymo can demonstrate that it has taken “effective corrective actions” to address the deficiencies.
Waymo spokesperson Dana Gallagher told TechCrunch the company has temporarily restricted freeway operations across its other operating markets to evaluate its performance.
“Safety is at the foundation of everything we do,” Gallagher said in a statement. “Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”
Waymo began offering freeway rides in late 2025 , a commercial milestone that has been central to its expansion in major metro areas. Freeway access allows Waymo to connect riders to airports and other destinations more efficiently, slashing travel times by avoiding slower surface streets.
That has been particularly important in the San Francisco Bay Area because Waymo’s service area stretches from the city south to Silicon Valley. Freeway access has dramatically shortened trips across the Peninsula that previously took 45 minutes or more than an hour.
In May, Waymo abruptly stopped operating on highways. The company didn’t cite a specific reason at the time, but several social media posts showed Waymo robotaxis driving through traffic cones and struggling to navigate construction zones.
Waymo robotaxis returned to freeways in July after the company said it updated the self-driving software system to improve performance around freeway construction zones.

Disruption at US intelligence agency comes amid questions over recent outages in air travel, communications services.
The United States National Security Agency (NSA) has said an outage affecting its internal communications network was due to “routine maintenance”, following a report by CNN.
The report, published on Tuesday and citing six unnamed sources, said there was no evidence that the outage was the result of a cyberattack. The incident follows a series of outages that have gone without explanation in recent days.
The network, known as NSA Net, allows employees of the US surveillance agency to share highly classified information internally, CNN said.
A spokesperson for the NSA downplayed the outage in a statement to Al Jazeera.
“The National Security Agency experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance,” the statement said. “While some internal systems were affected, mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational, and our ability to defend national security continues. NSA’s infrastructure is designed with multiple layers of redundancy to maintain operations during planned maintenance or unexpected events.”
The reported network disruption at the NSA follows several other major outages that have affected communication and transportation services in the US.
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) temporarily halted all takeoffs in the country on Friday, claiming that a system upgrade caused a flight communication overload. The ground stop, which lasted more than four hours, was called out of an “abundance of caution”, it explained.
The tech giant Microsoft also announced that services such as Outlook and Teams were down last week.
More recently, on Monday, outages hit major banks, and United Airlines briefly suffered a system disruption that delayed some departing flights.
US President Donald Trump has played down the seriousness of those outages.
“Things like that happen,” Trump told reporters on Tuesday. “It’s fine.”

Waymo self-driving taxis are no longer driving on highways after the California Department of Motor Vehicles banned its vehicles from state freeway operations. The ban, which the DMV says began on November 11, comes after the department determined that Waymo ’s freeway driving poses “an imminent hazard to public safety.”
In response, Waymo says it has stopped highway driving in all of its markets. The company may continue testing its vehicles on non-California highways with safety operators behind the wheels.
The ban follows two recent concerning incidents, California DMV spokesperson Jonathan Groveman wrote in a statement. In one, three Waymos entered an active highway construction closure on Route 101 on the San Francisco Peninsula. The other was captured in a viral video showing a Waymo vehicle interfering with California Highway Patrol cars on a San Francisco highway as they tried to enforce a “traffic break” as workers cleared debris from the crash.
Groveman said the California ban will remain in place until Waymo has proved that it has “taken effective corrective actions to address the deficiencies" that led to the incidents. It’s unclear how long that process will take.
In a written statement to WIRED, Waymo spokesperson Dana Gallagher said the company is “working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations." Waymo vehicles will continue to operate on surface streets in the 15 metros where it offers taxi service, including portions of Los Angeles, San Diego, and the San Francisco Bay Area.
This is the second time Waymo has publicly restricted its freeway operations after beginning to transport passengers on them last year . In June, the company recalled its software after federal regulators found that its system failed to recognize highway construction zones. Regulators with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) cited several incidents in April and May in which Waymo cars drove past ramp closure signs and into active lane closures. The events did not lead to collisions or injuries.
The NHTSA did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Last week, the agency said it was examining whether another Waymo recall software fix had actually solved its robotaxis’ safety issues. This recall, which occurred last December, was tied to incidents in which Waymo cars repeatedly drove by stopped school buses with their lights on and/or stop arms extended .
Self-driving cars have struggled with construction zones for at least a decade . The zones can look and be arranged differently based on what sort of construction is being done, and where. While humans can easily understand bollards, placards, and blinking arrows, the lack of hard-and-fast rules has proven difficult to reliably program into driving software. The issue is especially hazardous at high freeway speeds, where workers exist alongside fast-moving car traffic.

The United States has confirmed it is investigating computing company Megaspeed, suspecting it of violating US export controls by helping to ship tech giant Nvidia's chips to China.
In a joint statement, the US Department of Justice and Department of Commerce said they had been investigating Singapore-based firm Megaspeed since 2024.
It comes after questions were raised about the possibility high-end AI chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.
Concerns emerged in recent weeks after Nvidia founder Jensen Huang revealed he had an extramarital affair , allegedly with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. US authorities suspect her of spying for Beijing, which China denies.
Jensen Huang resigned from his role as chief executive last week following revelations he had two affairs.
Megaspeed is the biggest buyer of Nvidia chips in South East Asia and is suspected of helping divert advanced chips to China. The Singapore-based company said on Sunday it had launched an internal investigation into its business.
The justice and commerce departments said on Monday that "it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information" regarding the investigation.
Laying out a timeline, it said it began investigating Megaspeed in 2024 "for potential export control violations".
In May 2025, Department of Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia "concerning direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed". In June 2025, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its 'no sell' list.
Agents from the Bureau of Industry and Security, in conjunction with Singaporean law enforcement officials, then conducted an on-site check at Megaspeed that month and interviewed Alice Huang, who was chief executive at the time.
Alice Huang and Jensen Huang pictured together in Taiwan in June 2024
Following this enforcement action, the Department of Justice took the lead role in the criminal investigation of Megaspeed.
The Nvidia scandal has created tensions between the US Treasury and Commerce departments over shipments of high-end chips to Megaspeed.
On Friday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed the US Commerce Department, led by Howard Lutnick, for failing to properly oversee the export of the chips.
Lutnick has been called to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month over his department's role in allowing Nvidia to export its advanced chips.
While Singapore does not prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to companies abroad, such moves can breach US export controls.
Huang has agreed to testify in Congress, including before the House Select Committee on China to discuss whether US national security was compromised by his affair.
The White House said on Monday it would further restrict China's access to AI chips from firms like Nvidia.
The reported affairs by Jensen Huang created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms - a major company in the AI industry and central to the US as it competes with China for dominance.
Trump downplays warnings of AI risks, citing rivalry with China
In the statement, the US government said it would "bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred".
They added: "Sensitive technologies like semiconductors are among the most valuable and strategic assets of the US economy, and the Department of Justice and the Department of Commerce will remain vigilant in pursuing justice for those who want to compromise America's technological edge."

Nvidia has created a board-level committee for national security and export control. This follows the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang over extramarital affairs, allegedly including one with a Chinese intelligence asset.
Nvidia on Tuesday said it had created a board-level national security and export-control committee.
This follows the scandal surrounding former CEO Jensen Huang , who resigned last week over extramarital affairs , including one with a woman suspected of spying for China and working to help ensure higher quality chips crucial to AI development made it to the Chinese market.
The events have heightened oversight of the US tech giant and its importance to national security, as well as wiping several hundred billion dollars off the stock market valuation of what investors treat as the world's most valuable company in the space of a month.
Since Huang's resignation, some investors — including Elon Musk and Donald Trump — have voiced concern that his departure could leave Nvidia and America's AI sector in peril and are now calling for his return. Huang on Tuesday, expressed regret for "serious mistakes" in his personal life before declaring he would be "honored" to return if the company's board of directors thought that was "in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America."
Nvidia is calling the new group its National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee.
Suzanne Nora Johnson, a former vice chair at Goldman Sachs, will chair the committee, joined by fellow directors Stephen Neal, a former CEO of a law firm, John Dabiri, a professor of aeronautics and mechanical engineering at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech).
The committee will meet at least once every quarter. It will also incorporate independent legal, national security and trade compliance experts.
Nvidia already has a lower-level National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team; these groups will report to the board-level committee.
"We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation," Board Chair Harvey Jones said in a statement.
The company did not explicitly link the decision to November's developments and Huang's rapid fall from grace , but the timing seemed conspicuous.
The decision was announced hours ahead of Nvidia publishing its third-quarter results, with its still-stratospheric share price having fallen roughly 28% in the past month.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
US President Donald Trump , whom Huang was influential in persuading to allow the export of better-quality Nvidia chips to China than other US companies and officials deemed prudent, welcomed Nvidia's move on arrival in the Philippines on Tuesday.
"Yes, that's a good idea. It's a great company," he said during a photo opportunity at a Manila meeting with the other "Quad" leaders from Australia, India and Japan. "It's a great idea."
Trump reportedly owned Nvidia stock worth tens of millions of dollars before the share price fell. He also owns shares in other big tech companies.
Huang resigned last week after admitting to extramarital affairs in a message to Nvidia employees. This followed widespread reports, seemingly based on US and other intelligence, that one of the affairs was with a woman who used to lead a Singapore-based cloud computing company.
That company, Megaspseed International , is a major Nvidia client and is suspected of diverting advanced chips to China in violation of US export controls. Intelligence officials also suspect Huang's partner of being an asset of Chinese intelligence services.
The reporting on the case also seems to show these suspicions had been known to US officials and other countries, including Singapore, for roughly a year.

Bezos said that he was immediately drawn to Robert Pattinson’s performance during screen tests.
Robert Pattinson’s casting as James Bond made enough sense given his recent work with director Denis Villeneuve, who’s making the franchise’s next film over at Amazon. But it turns out that Amazon founder Jeff Bezos played a significant role in making the final decision, too.
During Semafor ’s Silicon Valley and the World conference today, Bezos said that he was “heavily involved” in the process of casting the newest 007:
We ran a really tight process and we made the final decision on Friday. There was a big group initially, and we down-selected to five finalists. Then we did real old-fashioned screen tests of those five finalists, and it was really interesting — full costume, real sets, other actors. We did three different scenes with each of the five finalists, and then we got together on Friday to spend a couple of hours looking at all those screening tests, and reviewing all of that. And all of the actors were extraordinarily talented.
By the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing, but there was something special about Rob Pattinson and his performances. It was kind of immediately undebated. Denis — the director — we all sort of gravitated to Rob. By the way, initially, I would say we were slightly biased a little against him, just because he’s already so famous. We sort of thought, ‘maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown.’ But in the screen test, it was so obvious. He is James Bond.
It’s not exactly surprising that a studio leader would want to have a say in casting the new face for one of their most lucrative franchises. But with Bezos being so hands-on, one can only image what this new era of Bond films will look and feel like once Amazon starts releasing them in theaters.

Anthropic on Tuesday disclosed more details about the biggest investment agreements with major cloud providers Amazon and Google.
While we already knew that Amazon stood to make a killing on its Anthropic investments from the IPO, Anthropic revealed that Amazon’s total stake will come in at just shy of 15% (14.7% to be exact).
Even more interesting is that Amazon could have, if it wished, owned an even bigger share of the company. When Amazon invested billions in Anthropic in 2023 and 2024 (long before Claude Code took the enterprise world by storm, back in the day when Anthropic looked like it would forever be a speck in OpenAI’s shadow), the cloud giant obtained promissory notes that could convert into equity.
These notes carry conversion prices of about $2.09 or $5.05 per share, depending on the year of investment. Amazon has opted to convert a chunk of them as part of the IPO into a special class of non-voting shares that will give it about 15% ownership. (The shares can receive dividends and convert to standard voting Class A shares when sold, the filing says).
But it has also opted to hold on to billions of dollars’ worth of the notes for now. If it converted them all right now, it would own just under 24% of Anthropic (23.8% to be precise).
Google, meanwhile, will own just under 14% (13.7%), also in non-voting shares, which come from the conversion of notes, as well as the “private placement” sale of shares as part of this IPO. A group of major tech companies (AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC Partners) have agreed to buy $26 billion worth of this non-voting stock. Google and Nvidia each agreed to buy $10 billion worth.
So while a lot of investors stand to make billions of dollars in Anthropic’s IPO, Amazon is one of the biggest winners, and that doesn’t even count that AWS stands to earn from Anthropic’s commitment to spend more than $100 billion on its cloud services over the next decade.

Apple’s inroads on designing repairable devices seems to have been abandoned with the HomeView.
After finding recent versions of Apple’s iPads and HomePods much easier to disassemble for battery replacements or other repairs, iFixit assumed it would be the same story for Apple’s new HomeView hub that looks like a seven-inch tablet stuck to a smart speaker. The reality was much different and by the time they got the HomeView apart iFixit’s skilled techs had “ripped a connector, snapped a speaker in two, and put more force on the poor logic board than any of us were comfortable with.”
The tablet section of the HomeView proved to be the bigger challenge to disassemble as a result of some questionable decisions with Apple’s design. The glue used to secure the display in place “held on harder than on any Apple product we’ve opened recently,” iFixit says. And while Apple’s decision to turn the HomeView’s entire aluminum chassis into a heat sink was clever, the thermal bond between a heat shield and the device’s logic board made separating the two a “remarkably risky operation.” While these design decisions possibly streamlined assembly at a factory, the extensive use of glue makes servicing the HomeView incredibly difficult.
In an accompanying teardown video iFixit also reveals how much smaller the speaker drivers are in the wall-mounted version of the HomeView versus the tabletop option. Although both versions are priced at $299, the wall version costs a little more when you factor in the required mount that’s not included, leaving iFixit feeling that you’re getting less performance while spending more money.

The first shoes with Nike’s new Tuned Air technology will be available for runners starting in late 2027.
In 2024, Nike announced its Air Max 1000 that were manufactured using a 3D-printing process resulting in a shoe that had a uniform silhouette but varying areas of support and flexibility throughout. The company is now doing something similar with its iconic air-filled soles using its new Tuned Air technology . While previously the level of cushioning in Nike Air shoes was uniform across the entire sole, a new manufacturing process can produce multiple air pockets with varying levels of cushioning and stability.
Nike has been putting air pockets into its shoes for nearly 50 years as a way to increase comfort and cushioning while making them lighter. Its air pockets have even found their way into apparel as a way to improve insulation by trapping body heat, but Nike plans to use its new Tuned Air technology as a way to customize the cushioning experience in its shoes and tailor them to specific athletes and sports. The first shoes featuring the technology are expected to arrive in late 2027 and will be targeted at runners.
While one of Nike’s earliest successes was track shoes with a grip design inspired by a waffle iron , the company credits the “vibrant colors on magazine covers” as the inspiration for its latest shoe technology. A Tuned Air sole is manufactured using a “proprietary digital print and selective lamination process” where an ink is applied in specific patterns that define where the layers bond to each other. This process can be used to create internal pockets in an unlimited combination of shapes and sizes, and by fine-tuning how much air is in each of those pockets, some parts of the sole can feel firmer while others feel softer.
The Tuned Air technology will not only allow Nike to highly customize the fit and feel of air sole shoes for different sports, it will also help keep the benefits of the custom tuning consistent across different sizes. The new manufacturing process will also help reduce the amount of time it takes Nike to go from a concept for a new shoe to a final design ready for production. “Prototypes that once took three weeks can now be made in three days,” the company claims in a release today. That gives Nike’s designers more time to refine new shoes, and more opportunity to experiment.

Was Google feeling a little left out of the recent wave of tech outages? The company took to X on Tuesday to announce that its Gmail service is actually running just fine. In a post, the company said it was not currently seeing evidence of a broad Gmail service disruption and reminded users they could always check Gmail’s real-time status on its online dashboard .
As it turns out, the company was trying to head off reports of a Gmail outage that began circulating on X on Tuesday around the same time that Apple was seeing a number of verified outages of its own . While some posts on the social network suggested Gmail was experiencing a disruption, others said they were not having any problems.
The concerns seemed to stem from an X post by Downdetector, a crowdsourced website where users can report service disruptions themselves and see if others are having problems. Downdetector is not an official source for verifying or understanding the true scope of internet outages, and as people become more concerned about possible cyberattacks, the site’s data may become less valuable over time if every minor glitch and hiccup is reported as an “outage” by non-technical users.
The fact that Google had to announce it was not having an outage speaks to the growing anxiety around the reliability of major tech services. Over the past week, Apple and Microsoft experienced outages, an FAA network failure led to a nationwide ground stop, and some banks and airlines also reported disruptions.
However, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said on Fox Business Tuesday that the U.S. is not currently facing coordinated cyberattacks. He told the outlet, “We do not see the indicia of a coordinated cyberattack — let me just be clear about that — and we do not see the indicia of state-sponsored activity here.”
Instead, Clayton attributed the rise in issues to businesses patching their systems. The patching may be a downstream effect of AI, as newer models have become increasingly adept at uncovering previously unknown vulnerabilities. “They’re upgrading them, they’re putting patches in place,” he said, adding that this is happening at “a much larger scale” than before.
As a result, some of the systems are “not coming back as expected in all cases,” he added.

Meta’s chief AI officer posted an AI video of a top competitor. It’s allowed under Meta’s AI policy.
Instagram is filled with people posting deepfaked content — including, as of late, from one of Meta’s most prominent executives.
Earlier in November, Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, shared a short clip to promote Muse, the company’s consumer AI agent. In the AI-generated clip, Wang, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, and Jolly, the anthropomorphic mascot of Muse, are on a four-way video call. When Altman joins the call he’s dressed like Jolly, wearing a furry hooded suit and face paint to look like the cutesy character. The clip is captioned “When the homies meet about openai product strategy,” a reference to the AI agent race and the recent popularity of Muse.
Just a few years ago, AI content portraying real people led to strong public statements rebuking the use of the technology to imitate humans. In some cases legal action was threatened . Now, AI content has become part of the texture of a new reality, especially on social media. Leading up to the midterm elections, for example, political groups ran millions of dollars’ worth of AI-generated ads attacking opponents.
Wang has been doing a lot of what some have described as “anti-PR” to promote Muse, tweeting hundreds of times and referring to more traditional marketers as “corposlops.” Still, a major tech executive posting an AI video of a competitor is notable, especially on a platform that’s been criticized recently over AI-generated content. After an AI-generated image of actress Mia Goth gained traction in October, the Pearl star’s representative told The Verge it was “incomprehensible” that Instagram allowed the image to spread instead of focusing on the “protection and integrity of a public figure’s likeness.” Other celebrities, including Scarlett Johansson, are regularly the subject of sexualized AI imagery; Meta has removed some accounts in the past that it found to be posing as someone else and using their likeness.
Meta requires AI-generated videos depicting people to be labeled as AI, like Wang’s post is. Static images, however, have no such requirement, meaning the AI image of Goth had no disclosure. To make matters worse, the image was shared by a fan account with a blue verification badge given by Instagram.
Reached for comment, Meta spokesperson Tracy Clayton noted that Wang’s post is labeled as AI content. Clayton also pointed out that Altman has made his likeness available for AI content generation, as when OpenAI launched its Sora app (and it was quickly flooded with fake Altman videos). OpenAI didn’t respond to requests for comment.

Model ML, yeni yatırımı Londra ve New York'taki araştırma ve mühendislik ekiplerini büyütmek, ürün geliştirme çalışmalarını hızlandırmak ve platformun daha fazla müşteride kullanılmasını sağlamak için değerlendirecek. Şirket bu yıl Paris, Madrid, Tokyo, Singapur ve Dubai 'de de ofis açtı.

Malware cocktail delivers cryptocurrency theft payloads and iOS exploits, among other things.
Hundreds of websites using the Optimizely website personalization platform served unsuspecting visitors a potent malware cocktail that targeted cryptocurrency wallets, stole payment card data, cookies, and screenshots, and delivered exploit kits for infecting iPhones and iPads, researchers said Tuesday.
ReportURI said it identified 178 websites—including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce—that were affected. JavaScript digitally signed by Optimizely and then loaded into customer pages had been modified to include malicious components that attempted to infect visitor devices with multiple payloads. When wares were installed successfully, they swapped user cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attackers. Other components skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and, on iPhones and iPads, delivered iOS exploit kits known as Coruna and DarkSword.
Optimizely serves JavaScript “snippets” that include both company code and code that is provided by each customer. The JavaScript, which can be served directly from Optimizely or from a customer endpoint, runs on every page the customer serves. Somehow, the attackers wrote their own code into a portion of each affected customer’s JavaScript and then delivered it from cdn.optimizely.com. A valid certificate for that domain signed the JavaScript.
ReportURI researcher Scott Helme said the delivery mechanism wasn’t a CDN cache poisoning attack , which uses HTTP to cause a CDN to cache harmful responses. Instead, the attack relied on Optimizely’s legitimate infrastructure, including its domains, to serve the tainted code. Optimizely’s own customer JavaScript for the www.optimizely.com and login.optimizely.com URLs were also affected.
“We don’t know how the attacker got write access to so many unrelated customer projects: a compromised Optimizely system, a compromised credential with cross-customer access, or something else,” ReportURI Helme wrote. “That’s for Optimizely to explain.”
Optimizely representatives didn’t respond to questions sent by email.
The scripts were named track.js, and all four components became active at the same time. Devices that received the malicious code responded differently depending on their platform and what they were doing on the final page delivering it. Actions performed included:
1. Crypto wallet address swapping. The script searches for wallet addresses for nine different cryptocurrencies and, when found, replaces them with one of the attacker’s. ReportURI said funds have already been stolen from some people whose devices ran the code.
2. Card skimming. The script watches HTTP requests for payment card numbers, expiry dates, and CVVs. When all three are present, it sends them to https://1688360.cc/card.php. Cards entered in hosted payment iframes such as Stripe and Adyen were unaffected.
3. Cookie and screenshot theft. When the script swaps an address next to a wallet or payment wording, it sends the document.cookie, the original address it replaced, and a screenshot of the page to https://1688360.cc/hit.php.
4. The DarkSword and Coruna exploit kits for iOS. The kits are delivered through a file named boot.js served from 5vobauua3ojpklx.icu and eil786npto9u5bq.icu. The file delivers a hidden iframe that contains an exploit chain tailored to the iOS version being used. Coruna can infect iOS versions 13 to 17. DarkSword can infect versions 18.x. A separate chain for iOS 26 fingerprints devices but doesn’t appear to do anything else. Earlier this month , researchers saw hackers possibly linked to the Kremlin attempting to deliver DarkSword through multiple vectors, including a compromised web analytics service.
The list of sites that ReportURI found delivering the malicious scripts numbers 178, and as noted, includes many big names. It’s unclear if the list is exhaustive. Helme said in an interview that “Ars wasn’t affected as far as we saw, and I haven’t seen any other indications it was.” Website administrators can check both the ReportURI post and this one from security firm Cynet for indicators of compromise.
At the moment, there’s no information available on how successful the exploit chains were in installing the payloads. Beyond the bare-bones details above, more precise information about what versions of iOS were susceptible was also unavailable. These sorts of gaps are common in breaking news concerning mass malware attacks, because it takes time for researchers to sift through the evidence. Readers are encouraged to check back as new developments come to light.
The indicators may help end users determine if they are affected, but the skill required is likely out of reach for many.
texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/crz9:
Stretching across the Kerch Strait in the Black Sea, the Crimean Bridge was always a symbol: for Russia, a prestige project cementing its claim to sovereign Ukrainian territory, and for Ukraine, a hated piece of infrastructure emblematic of Moscow's occupation of the Crimean Peninsula.
A key section of the double-arched, 12-mile-long bridge now lies on the seabed, brought down by an arsenal of Ukrainian long-range weaponry in a seven-stage operation culminating in a dramatic collapse.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has said that the bridge "will be rebuilt, and it will be even better than before".
But eight years after its unveiling, the bridge has now become material proof of Kyiv's ability to pierce through Moscow's military defences to hit even its most treasured and protected structures.
The attack on the strategic Crimean Bridge was carried out gradually to cut across several layers of defence, Kyiv confirmed on Tuesday.
For several weeks Ukraine's Security Service and its General Staff gradually destroyed air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare assets, and other designated targets, President Volodymyr Zelensky said.
A significant strike had already been reported on 16 November , when drones hit the bridge at night. Traffic was paused briefly then reinstated, and although the arch over the road section was visibly damaged, the structure remained standing.
But that hit turned out to have been only the penultimate stage of a complex attack.
In the early hours of 17 November, the final strikes dealt a fatal blow to the weakened arch structure.
One verified video - filmed from a camera on board a Ukrainian-made Flamingo missile - shows the weapon approaching the main span of the bridge and heading towards the steel arches, with the footage freezing just before impact.
The Flamingo had potentially been modified to be controlled remotely, which improved its accuracy enough to strike the bridge supports, munitions expert Justin Bronk, from the Royal United Services Institute said.
The missile's "very heavy warhead" made it "more suitable" for attacking the bridge's reinforced concrete spans and supports, Bronk added.
Zelensky later confirmed that several types of missiles and drones had been employed in the attack, which led the massive road arch - weighing thousands of tonnes and measuring about 227m in length - to collapse into the strait.
Daylight images taken from the shores of Crimea to the north show a section about 200m (660ft) long of the tarmac was too dragged below into the sea.
This is clearly critical damage to the crossing. Far from just being a decorative feature of the bridge, the arch played a structural role, transferring loads and supporting the span and helping to ensure the stability of the entire structure.
The parallel arch supporting the railway section has remained standing, although it may also have been damaged. All traffic on the bridge was initially suspended, though trains were later allowed to resume running.
But the damage to the bridge's main span is "catastrophic", Colin Capriani, a structural engineer from Monash University in Melbourne, Australia, told BBC Verify. It was "very hard to envisage" how the bridge could be rebuilt given it is clearly well within range of Ukrainian weaponry, Capriani added.
Major attacks in 2022 and 2023 had already caused serious damage to the road spans of the bridge, but the structure survived.
The difference this time is "the most critical and vulnerable part of the bridge has been hit", said David MacKenzie of engineering consultancy COWI, adding that "although the wreckage of the bridge can be cleared fairly quickly, reinstating full road traffic will take over a year".
Moscow uses Crimea as a military base, with airbases, troop concentrations, training grounds and artillery stockpiles. From there it also carries out strikes on the rest of the country and resupplies its troops in southern Ukraine.
The attack comes after a summer of frequent strikes on Crimea, dictated by Ukraine's stated goal of cutting the peninsula off from Russia. At the time, Kyiv vowed to turn the Crimean Peninsula "into an island".
Now - although it is too early to speak of a complete blockade of Crimea – the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis has increased significantly.
There is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of the Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions. However, Ukraine has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar, which has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo.
Moscow can also still utilise the ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited - and anything on the Black Sea has become vulnerable to attack. Resupplying Crimea by sea is risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area.
In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge - particularly its enormous arch - may have blocked the shipping channel. This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for ports in the Sea of Azov, including the occupied cities of Mariupol and Berdyansk.
Away from the operational value of the damage to the bridge, the symbolic significance remains.
In 2018, Putin triumphantly drove over the bridge representing the unification of Russia and Crimea in a Russian-made truck. That section of the road now lies on the seabed.
Nearly five years since he launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Putin continues to wreak destruction on Ukraine's civilian population, but his most prized symbols of power are increasingly threatened by Kyiv's reach.

President Donald Trump said Tuesday that US authorities take "very seriously" any possible threat to Washington, following reports Iran was planning to target officials, possibly with a radioactive bomb.
Asked about the potential threat during a visit to the Philippines , Trump said: "If there is (such a threat), they will pay a price the likes of which no other country has ever paid before."
"I hope it's not, but we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy."
CNN, citing seven anonymous US officials, reported that US intelligence indicated that Iran was preparing to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb in Washington.
The report said the sources characterised Iran's plans as "an effort to give itself options rather than an indicator of an imminent attack ".
A dirty bomb is a conventional explosive laced with chemical or radioactive materials.
Read more Trump says deal with Tehran 'could happen' amid 'intensive' talks
Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei dismissed the report as "fabricated", suggesting Washington was "seeking to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs".
"Step by step, they are attempting to manufacture a veneer of legitimacy for further aggression and atrocities," Baqaei wrote on X.
Baqaei also criticised a recent New York Times article which said, citing analysts, that some dams, pipelines and water tunnels in Iran "may have been developed to support the country's military buildup".
Iran's top negotiator in talks with the United States, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, posted a link to the same article on X, saying: "Prepping the next round on civilian infra(structure), their 'experts' tell NYT: 'dams near Iran's missile sites are dual-use'" – meaning they have both civilian and military application.
"Cool. New rule: Any dam, port, or power plant near a US or Israeli base is dual-use. We'll apply your logic consistently and even-handedly," Ghalibaf added.
Negotiations between the United States and Iran to end their war have stalled, and Iran recently targeted US infrastructure in the Middle East .
Mediator Qatar called for restraint on Tuesday "to avoid any escalation that could undermine negotiation efforts".

US officials ‘debate whether Iran can or will attempt to execute’ plot to detonate a ‘dirty bomb’, report says
Donald Trump has claimed the US is “looking into” whether Iran is developing plans to detonate a so-called “dirty bomb” in Washington, even as the White House said there were “no credible threats” at this time.
Trump said his administration takes the idea “very seriously”
After a CNN report , citing seven unnamed US officials, that new US intelligence suggested Iran was working on plans that would use a dirty bomb, which combines conventional explosives with radioactive material, or a chemical weapon against senior Trump administration officials.
The report noted, however, that US officials “continue to debate whether Iran can or will attempt to execute such a plot”.
The US president’s war on Iran is deeply unpopular among Americans. His Republican party was widely rejected by voters in the midterm elections, in which the GOP lost control of the Senate and House of Representatives.
Asked in the Philippines on Tuesday if there was reason to believe that such an Iranian attack was imminent, Trump said: “If there is, they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before. I hope it’s not, but we take it very seriously because they happen to ​be crazy.”
Lauren Bis, a White House spokesperson, said in a statement: “We remain vigilant monitoring any and all potential threats, but at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland.”
CNN cited the unnamed officials as saying that Tehran’s planning was an effort by Iran to “give itself options rather than an indicator of an imminent attack”, but the plans include specific locations and targets.
While the plans would signify that Iran is willing to escalate its tactics against the US, there is no evidence to suggest they will go ahead with them.
The US and Israel went to war with Iran starting in February, with early airstrikes killing Iranian officials, including the supreme leader, Ali Khamenei. Trump has repeatedly claimed the war will be over soon, but it has continued.
The US president has argued that US involvement in the war is necessary so that the country does not build nuclear weapons. Iran has blocked trade through the strait of Hormuz, creating rising fuel costs – and rattling the global economy.

Ulaştırma ve Altyapı Bakanı Abdulkadir Uraloğlu, Bakanlıkta HGS'ye ilişkin açıklama yaptı.
Son günlerde otoyol geçiş ücretleri ve HGS noktasında basında ve sosyal medyada bazı konuların gündeme geldiğini ifade eden Uraloğlu, süreci hem Bakanlık hem de Karayolları Genel Müdürlüğü (KGM) olarak yakından takip ettiklerini söyledi.
Uraloğlu, otoyol geçişlerinde HGS etiketi ve plaka olmak üzere iki şekilde tanımlama yapıldığını ve gerekli ücretlendirmelerin de bu tanımlama üzerinden gerçekleştiğini ifade etti.
HGS'si olmadığı durumlarda plaka üzerinden aracın tespit edilebildiğini belirten Uraloğlu, "Eskimiş etiketler ya da kirlenmiş, deforme olmuş plakalar varsa bu noktada bazı zorluklar yaşadığımız da oluyor. Mevcut sistemin yapay zeka destekli algılamasıyla beraber o plakayı tahmin ediyoruz, ona göre işlem yapıyoruz. Eğer burada bir yanılgı var ve bize bildirilmişse geriye doğru yapılmış olan bütün işlemlerin iptal edildiğini özellikle belirtmek isterim." dedi.
Bakan Uraloğlu, ihlalli geçiş söz konusu olduğunda 15 gün içinde vatandaşlara sisteme kayıtlı olan telefon numaraları üzerinden SMS ile bildirim yapıldığını, bunun bakiyenin yetersiz olması durumunda da gerçekleştiğini söyledi.
Vatandaşlara, tanımlı plakaya ait telefon numaralarını e-Devlet veya HGS sistemleri üzerinden güncelleme çağrısı yapan Uraloğlu, sözlerine şöyle devam etti:
"Biz 15 gün içinde gerekli bildirimi yaptık, eğer vatandaşımızın eksik bakiyesi varsa veya plakası hiç HGS abonesi olmamışsa, 'süre geçti, sen geçemezsin' demiyoruz. 15 gün içinde bir HGS hesabı açar öderse yine hiçbir problem yok. Bunlar olmadı, 15. günden 45. güne kadar bir kat ceza uygulamasıyla yine aynı süreç devam ediyor. Yani vatandaşımız 45. güne kadar eğer öderse bir kat ceza uygulaması söz konusu. 46. günden sonra özellikle kamu-özel işbirliği otoyollarında vatandaşa en az 15 gün içinde bir tebligatla bildirim yaparak bu süreci yine durdurmayı maksatlıyoruz. Eğer bu tebligata rağmen bir işlem, bir ödeme, bir başvuru yapılmamışsa bu sefer olay esasında bizim de istemediğimiz avukatla takip sürecine kadar gidiyor. Burada ben özellikle söylemek istiyorum, bütün bu dediklerim yapılmış da vatandaşa yine bir şekliyle gitmişse biz de birebir takip ediyoruz ve bu sefer ilgili işletmeciye idari yaptırımlar uygulama noktasında da tasarrufta bulunuyoruz. Dolayısıyla bizim vatandaşımızdan beklediğimiz, otoyoldan geçtiğini, hesap bakiyesini bilmesi ama bunlar yoksa bizim bildirimlerimiz üzerine mutlaka gereğini yapması. Esasında SMS'le de e-Devlet üzerinden de bildiriyoruz. Bunları vatandaşlarımız takip ederse, biz de vatandaşımız da rahat etmiş olur."
Bakan Uraloğlu, vatandaşların daha önce herhangi bir plakaya yönelik sorgulama yapabildiklerini ancak yakın zamanda bu sistemin değiştiğini bildirerek, "Kişisel Verileri Koruma Kurulunun (KVKK) yapılan şikayetler üzerine incelemesi sonucu, bunun doğru olmadığı, kişisel verilerinin ihlal edildiği noktasında bir karar alması ve o kararı da bizlere bildirmesi sonucu biz mecburen artık sadece ilgilinin bu sorgulamayı yapabilmesine imkan tanımış olduk. Öncesinde KGM'nin, PTT'nin, işletmecilerin sistemlerinden bunu yapabilirken artık KVKK kararıyla biz e-Devlet üzerinden yaptırma uygulamasına başladık. Dolayısıyla burada vatandaşımızın bir alışkanlığı, bir geçiş süreci söz konusu olduğu için tekrar böyle bir gündem oluşmuş oldu." dedi.
"Vatandaşlarımız daha duyarlı olsunlar. Biz de bu noktada daha ne yapılabilir, bunu özellikle sorguluyoruz. Amacımız vatandaşa asla ceza vermek, cezalandırmak değil. İşletmecileri, ihlaller avukata yani 4 kat cezaya gitmeden ne yapabiliriz konuşmak üzerine yarın tekrar bir topluyoruz. KGM koordinesinde yarın masaya oturulup değerlendirilecek ve toplantı yapılacak. Özellikle şunu da söylemek istiyorum, bu söylediğim çerçeve dışında bir davranışla karşılaşmış olan vatandaşlarımıza her türlü iletişim kapılarımız açık ve onlarla ilgili her türlü ilgi, alakayı göstereceğimizi özellikle belirtmek isterim."

Trump says US ‘looking into’ reported Iranian dirty bomb plot
President Donald Trump has said the US is taking "very seriously" the potential for any Iranian plot to attack Washington DC, after he was asked about a CNN report citing US intelligence assessments.
In the Philippines, where he attended the Asean Summit, Trump nodded when asked by a journalist about the report that Tehran was planning to detonate a so-called dirty bomb in the US capital and said: "We're looking into it."
CNN cited unnamed US intelligence officials suggesting Iran could target senior figures in Trump's administration with such an attack.
Iran called the claim "baseless." Concerns about dirty bombs grew after the 9/11 attacks in 2001, although no such attack has ever occurred.
Such a device would contain radioactive material - such as uranium - which would be scattered through the air when its conventional explosive detonated.
During his comments to reporters in Manila, Trump was asked whether there was reason to believe an attack was imminent.
"I hope it's not," he said, "but we take it very seriously because they [the Iranians] happen to be crazy."
The US president was answering questions from reporters in the Philippines
In a statement before Trump's comments, White House spokesperson Lauren Bis wrote: "We remain vigilant monitoring any and all potential threats, but at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland."
Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei rebutted the CNN article and other US reports.
He posted on X: "Those who initiated the aggression against Iran are now seeking to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs by manufacturing and disseminating baseless allegations."
Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's parliamentary speaker and chief negotiator in indirect talks with the US, was similarly dismissive of the CNN report.
"Same false flags, same war mongering, new logos," he posted on X.
Mick Mulroy, a former CIA paramilitary officer and deputy assistant defence secretary, told the BBC: "A dirty bomb is not difficult to make or deploy."
"Although it is not a weapon of mass destruction, it can be a weapon of mass disruption," he added.
Imran Bayoumi, a geostrategy expert with the Atlantic Council in Washington DC and former policy adviser to the defence department, said that it remains "unclear how serious" would be the threat of a supposed Iranian dirty bomb.
"But Iran has planned and threatened to attack the US in the past," he said. "It is also unclear why this report is becoming public now."
It comes as intelligence officials and members of the Trump administration seek congressional renewal of a key national security law.
Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (Fisa), which allows the US to ​spy on foreign nationals, expires next March.

US president Donald Trump issued a stern warning to Iran on Tuesday about the possibility that Tehran could be planning an attack involving a so-called dirty bomb or a chemical weapon in Washington DC, as reported by US broadcaster CNN citing what it called "sources familiar with the latest intelligence."
When asked whether the threat was imminent, Trump told reporters in Manila that "well, if there is, they will pay a price the likes of which no ​country has ever paid before."
Asked again whether there ​was reason to believe an attack was imminent, the US president replied that "I hope ‌it's ⁠not, but we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy," adding that "we are looking into it."
While Iran continues its fiery rethoric threatening with devastating consequences if attacked again, CNN reported that new US intelligence indicated that Tehran was developing plans to potentially detonate a dirty bomb or a chemical weapon in the US capital. However, according to the report, US officials were still divided over whether Iran has the capability to carry out such a plan or would actually move to execute it, and that officials were divided over the credibility of the intelligence.
The CNN report said that, according to its sources, the plans the United States has learned about were very specific and included locations and targets, prompting contingency planning, but CNN quoted one source as saying that "there is disagreement over whether they actually have the personnel in place to execute the plan." According to CNN's sources, Iran's capability to launch this kind of an attack has not grown, but what has changed is the Iranian incentive and that there was no evidence that Iran decided to move forward with its plans.
A dirty bomb is a weapon made of conventional explosives packaged with radioactive material that contaminates the environment through a non-nuclear explosion, affecting several city blocks or several kilometres.
White House spokesperson Lauren Bis downplayed the concerns by issuing a statement saying that the United States is "monitoring any and all potential threats, but at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland,” while US Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin told the US media that the dirty bomb threat "is not new".
The report was published the day after Israel's Mossad chief Roman Gofman returned from Washington where he reportedly met senior US officials, including CIA Director John Ratcliffe, to share Israel's latest intelligence on Iran. Israel's prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu has been insisting that the US and Israel must continue the military campaign against the Iranian regime.
According to multiple US media reports, senior members of the US administration have reportedly been moved over time to military compounds or protected government residences due to potential security threats.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed the allegations as "rubbish", stating in a post on X to “spare us the Iraq War-style propaganda, especially with Israeli fingerprints all over it, nobody is buying it.”
Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei called the allegations "baseless".
In a statement on X, Baghaei said that the dirty bomb plans allegations stem from a media narrative "designed to justify attacks on Iran's vital infrastructure."
The Iranian diplomat said that Tehran "considers the use of chemical weapons under any circumstances to be completely illegitimate and firmly rejects and explicitly denies the false and fabricated allegations made in this regard."
He warned that "Iran knows very well how to respond to any act of aggression and assures that this response will not be forgotten."
Tehran has been threatening the United States and Israel as well as any country supporting new military actions against Iran with a fiery response, including on their home territories.
These mounting threats come as the United States and Iran remain locked in an ongoing confrontation in the Strait of Hormuz with both sides increasing pressure to force concessions for most favourable terms in case of a peace deal.

A freight train runs on rails of a railway link of the Crimean Bridge connecting Russian mainland and the Crimean Peninsula over the Kerch Strait not far from Kerch, Crimea, on July 17, 2023. AP hide caption
KYIV, Ukraine — Ukrainian drones and missiles struck the vital Kerch Bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Tuesday, calling it an "unprecedented" operation as Russia reported that its forces downed a record number of Ukrainian drones for the second straight day.
Zelenskyy portrayed the bridge operation as a masterstroke following a weekslong effort by Ukrainian forces to gradually wear down Russian air defenses before bombarding the prized target with a barrage of missiles and drones overnight.
Zelenskyy didn't detail the damage, but the Ukrainian General Staff said that an arch and a span of the bridge's road section collapsed, severing the road link, while the railway line was still standing but with a damaged arch.
Russia's Investigative Committee, the nation's top criminal investigation agency, said the bridge was attacked by drones and sustained damage but didn't elaborate.
The Kerch Bridge is a crucial link in moving military and civilian supplies from Russia to Crimea and for supporting troops on the front line. The construction of the bridge, a potent symbol of Russia's illegal annexation of the peninsula in 2014, was inflammatory to Ukrainians.
"The symbol of the occupation has cracked," the Ukrainian General Staff said in a statement.
Moscow's forces, meanwhile, fired ballistic missiles and drones at Kyiv, hitting two of the Ukrainian capital's main bridges and killing at least two people.
A recent escalation in aerial attacks came as Russia and Ukraine await a date for the next round of U.S.-mediated talks aimed at ending the war that began with Moscow's full-scale invasion of its neighbor on Feb. 24, 2022.
U.S. President Donald Trump says he plans to talk about the war in Ukraine during his highly anticipated meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in China this week.
The Kerch Bridge attack was the culmination of weeks of preparatory strikes over seven stages of the operation, Zelenskyy said on social media.
Ukrainian forces knocked out defense systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment and other designated targets before launching Monday night's final attack, he said.
Domestically developed long-range drones struck the bridge's road section during the night while Ukraine's Neptune missiles and other drones aimed at the rail section, he said. Precision-guided Flamingo missiles delivered the final blow, he said.
Zelenskyy and the Ukrainian military published videos showing what they said were the attacks and subsequent damage to the bridge, with part of the deck in the water and a fallen arch. The Associated Press wasn't able to verify the images.
The Russian-installed governor of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, said traffic across the bridge was halted but rail traffic was restored by Tuesday afternoon. He didn't mention any damage.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said that "there is no doubt that the bridge will be restored and will be even better than it was before."
Zelenskyy noted that Russia has battered Ukrainian infrastructure, especially the power grid, every day. There were significant power outages Tuesday in three Ukrainian regions, he said.
"We have repeatedly offered Russia steps toward de-escalation — and every proposal has been met with loud rejection," he said.
U.K. Defense Secretary Wes Streeting, meeting at NATO headquarters in Brussels with Ukraine's Western backers, said the Kerch Bridge strike was "another example of Ukrainian ingenuity and Ukraine's absolute determination to defend itself against Russian aggression."
The United Kingdom announced £240 million ($317 million) in air defense support for Ukraine this winter, including more than 1,000 short-range missiles and more than a dozen radars.
Russian air defenses downed 1,441 drones during a second straight night of major Ukrainian attacks, Russia's Defense Ministry said Tuesday.
That was a day after Russia said that it downed 1,336 Ukrainian drones in the highest number of interceptions it had reported so far during the war.
Elsewhere, authorities in Bashkortostan, a Russian region in the southern Ural Mountains, said that defenses repelled a "massive" drone attack on industrial zones in the cities of Ufa and Salavat. All plants there worked as usual, officials said.
However, independent news outlet Astra reported a huge fire at the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat oil refining and petrochemical complex in Bashkortostan, nearly 1,300 kilometers (800 miles) east of the Ukrainian border. The major petrochemical complex has been attacked a number of times before.
In Moscow, Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said that around 800 drones flew toward the Moscow region overnight. Most were downed far away, and 321 were shot down as they approached the Russian capital.
Workers cut electrical wires on the southern bridge, damaged in a Russian missile strike, in Kyiv, Ukraine, Tuesday. Evgeniy Maloletka/AP hide caption
Seven Russian ballistic missiles hit two of Kyiv's main bridges during the night, Zelenskyy said. Both were closed to traffic.
The Pivnichnyi and Pivdennyi bridges are key commuter routes across the Dnipro River connecting Kyiv's two banks. The left bank is largely residential with numerous apartment buildings and shopping malls. The old town and many government offices are on the right bank.
On Tuesday morning, long lines of traffic formed on a third bridge linking the two sides of the city.
Russian attacks damaged other infrastructure and started fires in four districts of the Ukrainian capital, officials said, as Moscow continued its campaign to make life difficult for Ukrainian civilians.
The Russian Defense Ministry said Tuesday that its forces overnight hit Ukraine's military industrial facilities, energy, transport and port infrastructure, as well as vessels used for Ukrainian armed forces.
Russian forces launched a combined attack on industrial facilities in three districts of the southern Ukraine region of Zaporizhzhia, killing two people and wounding 18 others and leaving a large number of consumers in the region without power, local authorities said.
Meanwhile, the negotiating teams of Ukraine, the United States, and European partners held a working video call Monday in which they discussed the results of recent talks in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, and the agenda for the next stage of negotiations, said Rustem Umerov, head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service.
"We aligned our positions and our next joint steps," Umerov said on Telegram following the conversation.
Representatives of France, Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy, Poland, NATO and the European Commission joined the conversation.
The United States was represented by envoys Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner, and Alexus Grynkewich, the commander of U.S. forces in Europe, Umerov said.
