Real Madrid reached an agreement with Manchester United earlier this month to sign JJ Gabriel; The teenager requested to leave United in September and has not trained with the club since; the 16-year-old and his camp are confident there is a clear pathway to the first team at Real Madrid
JJ Gabriel has announced he is leaving Manchester United as he looks forward to his "next chapter" at Real Madrid.
Sky Sports News revealed earlier this month that Real have reached an agreement to sign the 16-year-old prodigy from United.
One source has told Sky Sports News a deal to take Gabriel to Real Madrid could be finalised in the next two to three days.
Gabriel is registered with Manchester United's academy until the end of the season but Real Madrid are intending to sign him in January.
There is a FIFA loophole that allows European clubs to tie down young players to professional contracts if they have a European passport which Gabriel qualifies for through both parents.
In a farewell post on Instagram he said: "Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020. as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams.
"Here I grew as a player and as a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award.
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
"You gave me moments I'll always treasure. To every coach, every member of staff, to my team-mates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.
"As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything. JJ."
Gabriel did not make a competitive first-team appearance for United, but did make a senior appearance in United's pre-season friendly defeat to AC Milan this summer.
The teenager requested to leave United in September and has not trained with the club since. When Gabriel's camp made it clear he wanted to move on, they asked to be de-registered immediately for the player to become a free agent.
Sky Sports News understands a big factor as to why Gabriel is leaning towards a move to Real Madrid is because he and his camp are confident there is a clear pathway to the first team at the Bernebeu.
Follow Sky Sports on WhatsApp for the latest sports news, videos, features, analysis and much more
"Those on the outside of Carrington's walls will understandably view Gabriel's impending departure as a major blow for Manchester United. The reality, however, is that it has been expected for some time. "Gabriel and his family have no longstanding ties to United as a club. He was not born and raised in the north of England, where a sense of local connection might have carried greater weight in his decision to stay. "Over the last 12 months, United have pulled out all the stops to convince Gabriel and his family that there was a pathway to the first team. They met Sir Alex Ferguson, Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick. Gabriel also trained with the senior squad and made his first-team debut at the age of 15 against Atletico Madrid in pre-season. "Ultimately, it was not enough to keep him at the club. As disappointing as it will be to lose a talent of Gabriel's calibre, United will no longer have to make further concessions to accommodate a young player and his family - a situation that can risk upsetting the balance of an entire academy system. "There is a wider consideration, too. Parents and agents connected to other academy players will inevitably take note when they see one individual receive such tailored treatment. It can create expectations that are difficult for a club to manage across its youth system. "This situation now appears to be reaching its conclusion. But the focus will soon shift to the 16-year-old himself. His talent is undeniable, but will the circus surrounding his exit become a hindrance to his development, or will it prove to be little more than a footnote in what could be a long and illustrious career? "Time will tell. And I imagine Jose Mourinho will have something to say about it, too."
"This kid's a good player. He could have been a superstar. Man Utd will be gutted.
"This rule has got to change. I think it's because his mum and dad have got an Irish passport that he's allowed to go abroad. And that needs to change.
"Manchester United have worked on this kid, made him the player he is. Obviously, he'd have been gifted at the same time.
"The thing is, he's going to Real Madrid. I said Manchester United are one of the biggest clubs in the world. He's going to the biggest club in the world. It's not like there's not a player in the world who wouldn't go to Real Madrid.
"You ask any player who's playing in the Premier League, if Real Madrid come for you, it's very rare you turn them down. Great opportunity for the kid."

Arsenal have paid tribute to Peter Storey, a key member of their 1971 Double-winning team, after the death of the former England midfielder at the age of 81.
Storey was part of the Bertie Mee team that secured the First Division title and FA Cup in a season that remains one of the most celebrated in Arsenal’s history and played 501 times for the club. That places him eighth on their appearances list.
Storey, who represented England on 19 occasions from 1971-73, earned respect for his uncompromising approach and versatility, also featuring at right-back.
Storey died in hospital after a short illness, surrounded by his family. Arsenal said: “Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 Double winner Peter Storey. All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time.”
Born in Surrey, Storey began his career at Arsenal and made his debut shortly after his 20th birthday in 1965. He is fondly remembered by the club’s fans for scoring a stoppage-time penalty in the 1971 FA Cup semi-final against Stoke that forced a replay and kept the Double dream alive.
Storey left for Fulham in 1977 and retired eight months later when his contract was cancelled, going on to own a pub in north London. He was later convicted of several criminal offences, including financing a plot to counterfeit gold coins and smuggling pornography. He released an autobiography , True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man, in September 2010.
Storey’s family said: “We are deeply grateful for the many kind messages, tributes and good wishes we have received. It has been a great comfort to see the affection and respect in which he was held by so many, both within the football community and beyond.”

Former Arsenal and England midfielder Peter Storey has died at the age of 81.
Storey made 501 appearances in all competitions for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, scoring 17 goals.
He was part of the Double-winning Arsenal team which secured the First Division title and FA Cup in 1970-71 under manager Bertie Mee.
"Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of double winner Peter Storey," Arsenal said in a statement.
"All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time.
"We will pay our respects to Peter at our forthcoming home match against Borussia Dortmund."
Surrey-born Storey joined Arsenal as an apprentice in 1961 and made his first-team debut against Leicester City in 1965, initially starting his career at right-back before being moved into midfield.
He is currently eighth on Arsenal 's list of all-time appearance holders and was capped 19 times by England, although he did not feature in a major tournament for the Three Lions.
Storey collected runners-up medals with Arsenal in the League Cup in 1967-68 and 1968-69 and in the FA Cup in 1971-72.
He joined Second Division Fulham on a free transfer in March 1977 and made 19 appearances for the Cottagers before his contract was terminated later that year and he retired.
However, Storey had something of a troubled life after his retirement from professional football.
He was convicted of running a brothel - for which he received a suspended prison sentence in 1979 - and was later jailed for three years for his involvement in a counterfeiting operation, then served another prison sentence in 1990 for attempting to smuggle pornographic videos into Britain.

Gianni Infantino has been president of Fifa since 2016 and is standing for re-election for a third time
Uefa has finally identified a candidate to take on Gianni Infantino in next year's Fifa presidential election.
Less than 48 hours before Wednesday night's deadline, European football's governing body announced that French Football Federation (FFF) president Philippe Diallo had received the unanimous support of its executive committee.
A late and surprise choice, Diallo said, "I think I have the experience, the convictions and the values which offer a credible alternative...I'm entering this campaign not just to provide a different voice, but to win."
But he is not the Frenchman some believe Uefa really wanted, as it tries to remove Infantino in the wake of his failed plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.
Senior figures in European football had hoped to persuade Arsene Wenger - Fifa's head of global development - to stand against his own boss. Some felt that only he possessed the credibility to pose a serious threat to Infantino's plans for a fourth term.
But after the former Arsenal manager chose not to proceed, Uefa had no choice but to seek an alternative.
So just how credible a challenger is Diallo? Does Infantino's position appear unassailable? And how could he still be stopped from winning another term?
Politicians, private jets and power - the life of a Fifa president
An administrator who has worked in French football since 1992 and became FFF president in 2023, Diallo is not a household name. But he has already shown he is prepared to stand up to Infantino.
In September, Diallo claimed he had "seriously damaged the image and unity of football", and said "trust has been broken" over the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) sell-off plot.
According to Uefa vice-president Laura McAllister, Diallo is a "candidate who can instigate real, meaningful and lasting reform" within the governing body.
"We've always made it very clear that our objectives and motivations are driving culture change. That means wide-ranging, systemic reform of football governance rather than simply the replacement of an individual leader," McAllister told BBC Sport.
"I've known Philippe since we were both elected to Uefa's executive committee, and he's an intelligent, honest, sharp-minded football person with an impressive experience of governance in one of the world's football power-houses. Most importantly, he is a person of integrity... Philippe is a fantastic advocate for the change agenda that football needs, and I know his campaign will reflect that."
Infantino remains the favourite to win a majority of the 211 votes, and is thought to have the support of most of Africa (54 members), Asia (47) and South America (10).
However, Uefa hopes that Diallo - whose father was a Senegalese boxing champion who represented France in the 1960 Olympics - could enjoy support in parts of Africa and beyond. He claims he already has the backing of countries beyond Europe.
Laura McAllister is a former captain of the Wales women's football team
While most of Europe's national associations are expected to vote for Diallo, it is clear that he was not Uefa's first choice. "I wasn't initially a candidate, but the insistence of my European colleagues led me to accept the offer", he admitted.
Uefa only approached Diallo about standing in the past week, and senior officials at some European national associations have also told BBC Sport they are frustrated with the failure to find a higher-profile candidate sooner.
Speaking anonymously, one said they only learned about Diallo's potential candidacy on Sunday, and that while they were supportive of him, "it would have been helpful if we'd had someone much earlier" and "a lot of eggs were put in the Wenger basket."
They also made the point that Diallo was yet to publish a manifesto, and questioned whether he could really win.
Another expressed similar sentiments, saying Diallo was a good man, but "not seen as a heavyweight". They claimed that Uefa had "lost the momentum. The process hasn't been great. I really hope they've got a rabbit to pull out of the hat."
McAllister is optimistic: "I have no doubt whatsoever that we will collectively mount a powerful campaign with the objective of winning the election next March". she said.
"The really critical period comes next, once candidate nominations close and eligibility checks are complete."
Despite high-profile critics like Germany manager Jurgen Klopp - who this week said "the opinion is unanimous that a change would make sense" - Infantino does appear to be in a position of strength.
As recently as August it all seemed very different when the heads of three confederations - Uefa, the Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf, which runs the game in North and Central America - signed a letter accusing the Fifa president of breaking trust "through deception".
Amid an increasingly acrimonious civil war, Infantino seemed vulnerable. But the revolt against him then suffered some setbacks.
Uefa called off a threatened boycott of Fifa competitions, and then potential rivals such as Concacaf chief Victor Montagliani decided not to stand. Aleksander Ceferin chose to stand for a fourth term as Uefa president rather than challenge Infantino directly.
Meanwhile, Infantino's position as the incumbent enabled him to embark on what has appeared to be a world tour, shoring up support. His chances of re-election received another major boost when he proposed to increase the amount of money handed out by Fifa for football development across the world by £2.6 billion.
Sheikh Salman, the head of the Asian Football Confederation, then performed a U-turn, endorsing Infantino, who soon after told the BBC he had the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football.
"I'm a professor of politics so I never assume that there's a runaway favourite to win any election", insists McAllister.
"There are plenty of twists and turns to come in this story between now and the election at Fifa's Congress next year.
"This is about structural change and a commitment to modernising the way in which football is governed so it benefits all who play and watch...that imperative will remain and we will hold the new president accountable for much-needed change."
"The current weaknesses of global football governance have been brutally exposed of late. This has helped coalesce and unite opposition to Gianni Infantino, but also to articulate the widely-held demands that things must change."
So with just four months until the presidential election, where could Infantino still run into difficulties?
Litigation is arguably the most obvious. As part of its wider plan to remove Infantino, Uefa has filed court documents in the US, which includes a potential criminal complaint against him in Switzerland for alleged financial mismanagement.
The legal action has not yet appeared to trouble him. But some senior figures in the European game remain hopeful it could still force Fifa to hand over evidence related to FFE that could prove damaging to Infantino's re-election prospects.
There is pressure from elsewhere in football. Fifa has already agreed to make "key documents" relating to the FFE plan available to members of its council. Infantino's critics believe this disclosure may reveal details that could increase the pressure on him before the election. Last month, the Norwegian Football Federation also submitted a three-part ethics complaint to Fifa regarding the awarding of a Peace Prize to US President Donald Trump, the Folarin Balogun case at the World Cup, and the FFE plot.
The Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections means scrutiny from beyond the sport too. Earlier this year, Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee launched an inquiry into Infantino's ties with Trump. In September, a spokeswoman said FIfa's co-operation with the investigation had been "woefully inadequate." But armed with extra powers, they could now…

Wayne Rooney has revealed he considered taking his own life while playing for Manchester United; this article discusses mental health and suicide, which some readers may find distressing; if you have been affected by this story, support and guidance are available at sky.com/viewersupport
Wayne Rooney has revealed there was a period in his Manchester United career where he contemplated suicide.
The former England striker revealed that, despite enjoying success on the pitch, he was struggling with his mental health off it. Newly married and a father to eldest son Kai, Rooney would sometimes spend two days drinking at home.
Speaking on the Life at the Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast, he admitted that, at his lowest point, he had contemplated taking his own life.
"I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with. Then I didn't want Kai seeing me like that, so that's why I'd hide away as well," Rooney said.
"I got to a place where you're contemplating suicide. You just didn't want to be around anyone. I didn't want to be see people in the streets. I didn't want to go into shops.
"I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else [I] really struggled with it."
Rooney, United's all-time record goalscorer, said the issues he faced occurred at the height of his Red Devils career.
"You don't want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it," he added.
"Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man if you like for doing that.
"I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because when I look back I was probably at the height of my career, I've just had a young son, I've just been married. It should be the happiest point in my life and it wasn't.
"It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking."
Rooney, who is currently featuring in ITV reality programme 'I'm A Celebrity… Get Me Out Of Here', credits his wife Coleen with helping him turn the tide.
"Coleen helped me massively. She could have walked away, it was that bad, but she stuck by me and helped me get through it," he said.

Philippe Diallo, Europe’s candidate to fight Gianni Infantino for the Fifa presidency, said he had received “strong signs of support from other continents” as he launched his campaign in Paris on Tuesday.
The French Football Federation president also said he had contacted Kozo Tashima, who announced his candidacy this month, and would try to convince him to “join forces”. Diallo did not indicate whether he would explicitly be asking Tashima to stand aside. “Our approaches are based on the same assessments and the same values,” he said.
Diallo revealed the first figure from Uefa to encourage him to mount a late challenge had been the Football Association chair, Debbie Hewitt. With strong European backing, the 63-year-old has secured 55 of the 106 votes needed to unseat Infantino, the favourite in March’s election.
“With the unanimous support of Uefa, I already have a large base of votes,” Diallo said. “It’s now up to me and my team to go and convince those on other continents. Since yesterday, I’ve had strong signs of support from other continents which will be revealed in the coming days.”
Diallo’s candidacy was ratified by the FFF’s executive committee on Tuesday, one day before the deadline to declare for the election. Tashima, the Japan FA’s honorary president, is the only other person to have said they will take on Infantino . “Initially I wasn’t running,” Diallo said, “but the insistence of my European colleagues, as well as others, led me to accept the proposal.”
Diallo has worked in French football since 1992, chairing the lobby group Union des Clubs Professionnels de Football for almost 30 years before joining the FFF in 2021. He was elected president two years later, having initially stepped up in an interim capacity .
He is also very familiar with the inner workings of Fifa, having been a judge in its dispute resolution chamber for more than two decades.
“I have the experience, the conviction and the values to make my candidacy a credible alternative to the current Fifa leadership,” he said. “I’m entering this campaign not just to provide a different voice, but to win. What has happened over the last few months has shocked the footballing world and does not match our vision for the future of football.”
Diallo, who formally withdrew the FFF’s support for Infantino in September, said he was “aware of the responsibility” of his candidacy: “I’m doing this to be in line with everything that we’ve been saying since this summer, and even before that.”
Diallo reiterated his criticism of Infantino and railed against what he described as “solitary governance” at Fifa. “The great issues of football are being decided behind the scenes, with no transparency, without consulting the stakeholders,” he said.
According to Diallo, recent events have “damaged football’s image, its credibility, and have introduced the poison of division”. He cited the Fifa Peace Prize , the lifting of Folarin Balogun’s red-card suspension during the World Cup, the extended half-time break during the final and the failed World Cup sell-off plan .
Diallo indicated he had not spoken with Infantino in months. “The last time I saw him was at the World Cup, when he came to a few France matches,” he said. “Unfortunately he didn’t take the opportunity to share some of his projects with us. I considered that to be an act of defiance.”
Diallo said he would go into detail on his manifesto on 6 December at the Euro 2028 qualifying draw in Belfast. “My vision is that of open governance,” he said. “It’s one where the authorities truly play their role and the president is in charge of vision and strategy but leaves the day-to-day management to the secretary general. I think that certain stakeholders, namely the clubs and players, need to be more directly involved.”

Nations League quarter-finals, semi-finals and final format explained, with draw for last eight on Friday after groups decided; England had already progressed to knockouts but won group with victory over Spain in Madrid on Sunday
England have topped their group in the Nations League after an incredible win over Spain - but who will they play in the last eight in March?
England's win over Spain in Madrid means they have finished top of the group.
That matters as the winners of the Nations League tier A groups are seeded for the quarter-final draw. They will play teams which have finished runners-up in other groups. They will also play the second leg of their quarter-final at home.
Belgium finished runners-up in Group A1, so they are a potential last-eight opponent for England.
Netherlands are another potential opponent as they finished second in Group A2 following their 5-0 loss to Germany, who topped the group.
Norway are the final team after they came from 2-0 down to beat Denmark 3-2 - and qualify for the quarter-finals at the Dane's expense.
The Three Lions cannot draw Spain in the quarters, as teams from the same group cannot face each other in the quarters, or France because they finished as Group A1 winners.
The draw for the last eight will take place on Friday at 11am UK time.
The quarter-finals will be two-leg ties, with the seeded group winners playing the second match at home.
The matches will take place in the March international break, with the first legs between March 25-27 and the second legs between March 28-30.
The Nations League Finals will then be held between June 9 and June 13, 2027.
The tournament will feature two semi-finals, a third-place play-off and the final, with four nations competing to be crowned champions of Europe.
The four semi-finalists will be invited to make bids to host the semi-finals and final.

Real Madrid'in 21 yaşındaki yıldızı Arda Güler için Paris Saint-Germain'in 200 milyon euroluk teklif hazırladığı iddia edildi. Böyle bir satış gerçekleşirse Fenerbahçe , bonservisten kalan yüzde 20'lik pay sayesinde kasasına yaklaşık 40 milyon euro koyacak.
İspanyol El Gol Digital'in haberine göre Fransa 'nın en büyük kulübü, Real Madrid'in genç orta sahasını kadrosuna katmak için 200 milyon euroluk bir teklifi masaya koymaya hazırlanıyor.
Dikkat çeken ikinci detay zamanlama. İddiaya göre Real Madrid ile Güler yeni sözleşme konusunda anlaşamazsa, PSG'nin teklifi kış transfer dönemine doğru çok daha ciddi bir hal alacak. 21 yaşındaki oyuncunun Madrid'deki geleceği, bu yüzden önümüzdeki haftaların en çok konuşulan transfer başlıklarından biri olmaya aday.
Maaş tarafındaki fark da büyük. Real Madrid'in Güler'e yıllık 8 milyon euroluk yeni bir sözleşme önerdiği, oyuncunun bu teklife henüz olumlu yanıt vermediği öne sürülüyor. PSG'nin ise yıllık 22 milyon euro ödemeyi göze aldığı iddia ediliyor. Yani iki teklif arasında yılda 14 milyon euroluk bir uçurum var.
Real Madrid cephesinden gelen haberler ise tek bir yöne işaret etmiyor. Ekim ayında Mundo Deportivo, Fabrizio Romano'ya dayandırdığı haberinde 2032'ye kadar uzatma anlaşmasının tamamlandığını yazmıştı. AS'den José Félix Díaz ise kulübün 2031'e kadar bir yenileme üzerinde çalıştığını aktarmıştı. Güler'in 8 milyon euroluk teklifi reddettiği bilgisi ise ESPN'e atfedildi.
Fenerbahçe 'nin bu hikâyedeki payı, 2023 yazında imzalanan transfer anlaşmasından geliyor. Güler, o dönem Real Madrid'e 20 milyon euro artı 10 milyon euro bonus olmak üzere toplam 30 milyon euroluk bonservis bedeliyle gitmiş, 6 yıllık sözleşme imzalamıştı. Sarı-lacivertliler anlaşmaya ileride yapılacak satıştan yüzde 20 pay alacakları maddesini de eklemişti.
Hesap basit: 200 milyon euroluk bir satışta bu oran 40 milyon euroya karşılık geliyor. Mayıs ayında yayımlanan bir habere göre 90 milyon euroluk bir satışta bile Fenerbahçe'nin payı yaklaşık 18 milyon euro olacaktı. Yani 2023'te kasaya giren paranın üzerine, aradan geçen yıllarda çok daha büyük bir ek gelir ihtimali doğdu.
Transfer iddialarının ortasında Güler'in sahadaki rakamları da dikkat çekiyor. 21 yaşındaki oyuncu, 2026/27 sezonunda Real Madrid formasıyla tüm kulvarlarda 14 maça çıktı, 4 gol attı ve 7 asist yaptı. Yani maç başına yarımdan fazla gol katkısı üretiyor.
Madrid yönetiminin 8 milyon euroluk yenileme teklifine henüz yanıt alamadığı, PSG'nin ise yıllık 22 milyon euroluk bir maaş paketiyle devreye girmeye hazırlandığı konuşuluyor. Güler ile Real Madrid arasındaki sözleşme görüşmelerinin kış transfer dönemine kadar sonuçlanıp sonuçlanmayacağı bekleniyor.

Northern Ireland are in the Nations League top-flight after topping their group after a draw in Hungary; Barnabas Varga ended Northern Ireland's proud record of not having conceded in this campaign but Justin Devenny equalised
Justin Devenny's superb strike saw Northern Ireland earn promotion to the top tier of the Nations League with a hard-fought 1-1 draw away to closest challengers Hungary in Budapest.
Barnabas Varga ended Northern Ireland's proud record of not having conceded in this campaign when he fired the hosts in front after 35 minutes - a goal that also sent Hungary to the top of the group.
But moments after Isaac Price had hit the post for Michael O'Neill's young side, Devenny smashed the ball into the top left-hand corner in the 65th minute to restore Northern Ireland's one-point advantage as group leaders.
The visitors were on the back foot for much of the first half, with Hungary captain Dominik Szoboszlai hitting the post, but O'Neill, serving a touchline ban in the stands as former captain Steven Davis led things from the touchline, orchestrated key substitutions.
Northern Ireland started with Patrick Kelly in place of the suspended Jamie Donley up front but brought on Josh Magennis at half-time before Kieran Morrison and Brodie Spencer soon followed to help the visitors become a much greater threat going forward.
Magennis' physical presence and the extra pace paid dividends as, just two years after earning promotion from League C, Northern Ireland completed an unbeaten campaign in Group B2 to secure their place at the top table of European football.
Without Donley, the lack of a clear outlet told in a first half that saw Hungary come forward time and again.
There was a big panic after five minutes following an uncharacteristic mistake from Pierce Charles, whose pass went straight to Bendeguez Bolla, a late change to the Hungary side, who whipped in a superb low cross from which skipper Szoboszlai struck the post.
Northern Ireland were pegged back but might have snatched the lead from a Ciaron Brown long throw in the 33rd minute. However, Tom Atcheson did not seem to realise how much space he had as he prodded a weak shot towards his Blackburn team-mate Balazs Toth.
Two minutes later Pierce Charles launched a long free-kick into the box. Brown went down under an Andras Schafer challenge, but as Northern Ireland appealed in vain for a penalty, Toth kicked it long. Trai Hume got his head to the ball but could not get it as far as Pierce Charles, allowing Varga to nip in and score.
O'Neill will have felt the frustration of his ban with his side trailing at half-time, but his changes worked regardless.
Terry Devlin, the matchwinner on Saturday, had already fired into the side-netting before Price's low strike from the edge of the box cannoned back off the post.
Four minutes later they were level. Hume's long throw almost fell for Shea Charles but instead sat up for Devenny to take a touch before thumping an unstoppable strike into the top corner.
As time ticked down, Hungary pushed forward in increasing desperation - with Rajmund Toth firing over late on - but Northern Ireland dug in with the defensive resilience which has been the cornerstone of this campaign.

Ancak oyuncudan veya dizinin yapım ekibinden konuya ilişkin herhangi bir resmi açıklama gelmedi. Şaşmaz'ın projeye dahil olup olmayacağı ve olası rolünün ne olacağı henüz bilinmiyor.
İddiayı dikkat çekici kılan ayrıntılardan biri de Yeraltı dizisinin senaryo ekibinde Necati Şaşmaz'ın kardeşi Raci Şaşmaz'ın bulunması.
Kurtlar Vadisi 'nin yaratıcı ekibinde de görev alan Raci Şaşmaz, yeni dizinin senaryosunu Berna Aruz ile birlikte kaleme alıyor.
Yeraltı dünyasındaki güç mücadelelerini konu alan yapım, hikayesi ve atmosferi nedeniyle Kurtlar Vadisi ile benzerlikler taşıdığı yönünde değerlendirmelere konu oluyor.
Yönetmenliğini Murat Öztürk'ün üstlendiği Yeraltı dizisi, Türkiye'deki suç örgütleri ve karteller arasındaki iktidar mücadelesini merkezine alıyor.
Çarşamba akşamları NOW TV ekranlarında izleyiciyle buluşan yapımın, yayın hayatına başlamasının ardından reyting sıralamasında üst basamaklara yükseldiği belirtiliyor.

Declan Rice has agreed a new long term-contract at Arsenal so can he continue to go from strength to strength? Jack Wilshere, his former team-mate at West Ham, tells Sky Sports Rice is "definitely in the conversation as one of the best midfielders in the world"
Arsenal's Kroenke family owners tend not to get involved in transfer dealings. But when it came to Declan Rice, and the prospect of spending £100m on a player for the first time, they needed to be sure that it was a sensible investment.
So, in the conference room at Arsenal's training ground, co-chair Josh Kroenke asked to be walked through the deal by Mikel Arteta, former sporting director Edu, then executive vice-chair Tim Lewis and now chief executive officer Richard Garlick.
"My eyebrows raised because I didn't know if we were in that phase just yet to go after a player like that," Kroenke recalled. He wanted to know what he would bring and how Arteta would use him.
Kroenke left the meeting in no doubt about the deal, either financially or in footballing terms. A club-record approach to West Ham was greenlit and Rice has of course gone on to prove an inspired addition, his new deal reflecting his importance.
"Declan Rice, we got him half price," is the refrain among Arsenal supporters. A player instrumental in their Premier League title success, who insisted "it's not done", then did more than anyone to drive them over the line, is now tied down for his peak years.
He has brought Arsenal even more than the club anticipated, arriving as a No 6 before being unshackled as a rampaging No 8, then reverting to a deeper role this season.
He scores, creates and dominates physically. His deadly set-piece delivery, honed to a world-class level, is another weapon.
"He is becoming a total player," said Arteta, who has even called on him at right-back. Of course, Rice filled in admirably in that role. "A total player has to be able to do as many things as possible and he has the capacity to do that," added Arteta.
Rice's adaptability and willingness to evolve his game have been themes of his time at Arsenal. The same traits were apparent to those who worked with him at West Ham, where he made an instant impression on his former team-mate Jack Wilshere.
"I love Declan, first of all a person," Wilshere tells Sky Sports. "I could see that straight away when I went in. He was very humble, his eyes were open, he wanted to learn, he would ask the right questions, and he just went from strength to strength.
"His footballing ability speaks for itself, but I wouldn't say he's someone who it came naturally to. He had to work on his right foot, on his left foot. But physically, he was always a beast and that would help him get out of certain situations."
Wilshere also noted the leadership qualities that have come to the fore at Arsenal. "Even when I went there and he was 19 or 20 and finding his way in the team, he had natural leadership and a natural aura about him that you could see," he says.

"He has a good understanding as well. When you look at players making big moves now, for me, one of the most important things around it is timing. I think Dec got his timing right.
"He spent a good few years at West Ham becoming a hero, becoming an important member of that team, trying to get that team up the table to finish high as possible. He won a trophy with them, and then he decided to go and compete for bigger things."
Wilshere and Rice crossed paths again following his move to Arsenal, where Wilshere, now head coach of Luton Town, was working as an academy coach and shadowing his old team-mate Arteta.
"I know how important he was to Mikel at that time when Mikel brought him in, and how he was going to be that shining light of the team who would always be present," he says.
"That's another thing that's really impressive about him: his robustness. He plays every single game. He dominates every single game physically."
Rice's record bears it out. Last season was his most demanding yet as he made 55 appearances in all competitions for Arsenal, many of them while managing hamstring nerve pain, before making a further eight for England at the World Cup during the summer.
He is an incredible athlete who continues to show remarkable resistance to injury. He has only missed five out of 119 Premier League games since his arrival at Arsenal. Only four outfield players have played more minutes in the competition in that timeframe.
His reliability is invaluable to Arteta and Rice continues to find ways to improve. Having moved back to the base of midfield this term, switching to the right side of the pivot to accommodate Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes, he has become notably more incisive with his passes.
His total of five assists is the highest of any Premier League player this season and it is notable that all of them have come in open-play.
According to Opta, Rice ranks second among Premier League players - and top among midfielders - for line-breaking passes this season, behind only Jan Paul van Hecke. He also ranks second only to Martin Odegaard for line-breaking passes in the final third.
A player once criticised for sideways passing is now averaging nearly twice as many line-breaking passes than last season, showing clear development in yet another area of his game.
The hope for Arsenal is that Rice will continue to unlock more levels after committing his future to the club. That is certainly the expectation from those who know him.
"I actually think there's more to come from Dec," adds Wilshere. "I've said it for a few years now. To be fair, he has started to add goals, but I still think he can add more with his physical ability, with his ability to strike the ball off his left foot, right foot.
"But he's already a top player and definitely in the conversation as one of the best midfielders in the world."

Match report as Wales lose final Nations League Group A4 game to 10-man Portugal in a 3-2 home defeat; Man Utd's Bruno Fernandes hit opener; Chelsea's Pedro Neto scored Portugal's second but was sent off in second half for two bookings in two minutes; Portugal finish top with Wales bottom
Wales ended their Nations League group campaign with a 3-2 defeat against 10-man Portugal in Cardiff after Chelsea's Pedro Neto was sent off.
Although there was little riding on the contest, with Wales guaranteed a League A relegation/promotion play-off in March and Portugal having qualified for the quarter-finals, the two sides produced an entertaining spectacle.
Portugal skipper Bruno Fernandes blasted the opener after 11 minutes, but that was immediately wiped out by David Brooks' ninth goal for Wales.
Sorba Thomas broke free to put Wales ahead before the break, but again there was a quickfire response as Neto pounced to restore parity.
Substitute Carlos Forbs stroked Portugal ahead in the final quarter, and the visitors had to negotiate the final 16 minutes a player short after Neto was sent off after receiving two yellow cards in the space of two minutes.
Wales finish bottom of League A4 with one win and five defeats, and end a disappointing 2026 with a solitary victory, three draws and six losses from 10 games.
Portugal, meanwhile, finish the campaign as group winners as they earned their first win since Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement .
Craig Bellamy's side had lost 1-0 in Lisbon in September in a game that was to prove Ronaldo's last for Portugal.
Ronaldo's subsequent retirement from international football probably had an impact on the attendance at Cardiff City Stadium, with some seats unfilled, despite the game being officially declared a sell-out.
There would be no clean sheet for Danny Ward on his 50th appearance as Joao Neves robbed Josh Sheehan and Fernandes lashed home from the edge of the box.
Wales responded immediately with Rubin Colwill twice involved, first setting up Harry Wilson for a shot Diogo Costa blocked with his legs and then Brooks, who swept home his ninth international goal, and second in two games.
Wales hit the front five minutes before the break after Brooks worked a one-two with Wilson before releasing Thomas, who advanced from his own half to slot past Costa.
The lead lasted three minutes as Neto lost Jay DaSilva from Trincao's cross to finish at the far post.
A breathless first half was not finished as Wilson hit the roof of the net from halfway with Costa retreating frantically, and the Leeds midfielder then forced a sprawling save from the Portugal goalkeeper.
Portugal regained the lead 20 minutes from time when Club Brugge winger Forbs - wearing Portugal's new-styled number seven shirt in the post-Ronaldo era - collected Ben Cabango's poor header and stepped inside Ben Davies to find the bottom corner.
Neto clattered into Brennan Johnson just one minute and 59 seconds after being booked, but Portugal held on for a fifth Nations League win to seal top spot.
"We knew in moments we were going to have to suffer due to the quality they have. The intensity wasn't there. We have a lot of players who don't play week in, week out a high-tempo game in such a short space of time. It's not ideal.
"We knew that at moments, when we win it, the spaces open. There were moments that worked really well. It summed up the group for us - really good moments for us; we make a mistake - at this level, these are normal things that happen.
"But also, that final moment. These teams have that profile to hurt you. At both ends, that last bit has caught us a bit in this group.
"Rubin Colwill is really good. There are times where he takes too many touches. You can't do that against this type of team. Five, six, seven - no! When he motors like he has, the ability to be a real top-end player. I'm very critical of him; I do love him.
"But I know there's more. That's why I wanted to play him in this A league. He's going to have to prove himself."
"For large parts, we played really well again. At times in the first half, we had to suffer. They're a great team full of world-class stars. At times in our shape, we were comfy.
"But look at our three goals. We're disappointed. But for large parts we were really, really good again.
"We knew from the start it was going to be tough. The first game in the group against Portugal, we showed we belong. Against Norway, we beat them. In large spells tonight, we were the better team.
"Going forward or defending the goal a bit better, that's what we've got to focus on. We're going toe-to-toe with these teams; our shape is good off the ball."
